We are developing an image slicer for an integral field unit, ROSIE IFU, to integrate with the IMACS spectrograph on the Magellan Baade Telescope at the Las Campanas Observatory. The device consists of a filter wheel and an image sensor, along with an acquisition software. The system comprises 9x9 pupils, arranged into 9 slices, each capturing a section of the sky. By processing the slices through a diffuser, we'll achieve a final resolution of 0.61 arcseconds per pixel. The project involves both hardware and software components. We've designed two diffrasers to optimize the illumination of the image sensor and the transmission of light through the device. Additionally, a custom-written software utility facilitates the seamless connection between the device's controller and the telescope's control system. Through diffraction-based imaging, the spatial information of the slices is accurately determined, allowing us to accurately determine their positions and orientations. The project has successfully demonstrated the integration of all components, including the diffusion-limited image slicer, and the in-telescope operation of the device.

In this paper, the carbon-carbon fusion research is revisited to incorporate the latest developments. Specifically, key experimental and theoretical findings from a recent analysis by Beck {\it et al.} (Eur. Phys. J. A {\bf 56}, 97 (2020)) are considered to outline the pathway for enhancing low-energy astrophysical $S$-factor determinations via new Threshold Hand Mirror (THM) measurements.

A crucial aspect in analyzing the bulk composition of Earth-like planets in other star systems is the process of devolatilisation that occurs due to high temperatures and pressures. Various models are available to study this process, however, a comprehensive comparison of them has been lacking until now. Our research aims to address this gap by examining the outcomes of different devolabilsation models and presenting a simplified framework that encapsulates the core mechanisms. By applying this framework to Earth and other planetary bodies in our solar system, as well as promising terrestrial candidates for life such as K2-18 b and Proxima b, we evaluate the impact of devolatilisation on the mass fraction of key volatile elements and the H2O content of these bodies. Our study highlights the significance of devolatilisation in shaping the structure and composition of planets, particularly in influencing the mass fraction of key elements and the H2O content. By utilizing this simplified model along with detailed numerical models, we hope to provide a more unified understanding of devolabilsation and its effects on planetary composition.

Deep neural networks (DNNs) have become a preferred method for wireless localization based on channel state information (CSI), utilizing raw CSI to learn location-specific features. Nevertheless, several studies demonstrate that CSI is prone to system disturbances and subtle environmental changes. Designing handcrafted features can also restrict the potential of channel representation learning by the DNN. This research suggests attention-based CSI for learning robust features. The proposed approach's effectiveness in improving localization accuracy with less training data is validated on several public datasets.

This paper presents a comprehensive framework for modal logic semantics by linking different types of logical meaning in the literature to the topological categories theory. Building on similar methods in categorical logic, we will thoroughly examine the relationship between the structural composition of the modal language, its various expansions, and the topological structures in categories, thus offering an abstract understanding of the underlying logical framework.

A graph's edge coloring can be described as assigning different colors to edges based on a specific distance criterion, effectively mirroring the requirements of a certain vertex coloring in a transformed version of the graph. This notion was initially proposed as an open problem by Faudree, Schelp, Gyárfás, and Tuza in 1990, assuming a bipartite graph of high enough girth and a specific limit on the number of edges per vertex could be colored using a certain number of colors, but in 2021 this was contested. Now, another example is given which also contests the third of a conjecture made by the same authors in 1990, assuming a hypergraph of high enough girth and a specific limit on the number of edges per vertex could be coloured using a certain number of colours.

We investigate functions defined on the vertices of the Hamming graphs H(n,q), focusing specifically on those with support contained in the direct sum of the eigenspaces U_i(n,q), U_{i+1}(n,q),..., U_j(n,q) where 0 ≤ i ≤ j ≤ n. Under certain conditions, specifically when n is greater than or equal to the sum of i and j, and when the size of the alphabet is 3 or greater, we identify the functions with minimum possible support and establish a characterization for those with such a minimum. In scenarios where n is less than the sum of i and j, but with a sufficiently large alphabet size of at least 4, we identify similar properties of functions.

COPASI is a widely-used simulation and analysis tool for biochemical networks and their dynamics, but users had to run it locally as a standalone application. To address this limitation, we have developed ShinyCOPASI, a web-based platform allowing users to interact with COPASI models through their web browser. Built with R using CoRC and Shiny, ShinyCOPASI mirrors COPASI's interface for seamless exploration and enables running tasks available in the original software within a browser. It offers a basic model upload feature and a server-loaded model option, providing web access to existing models. Users can access ShinyCOPASI at http://shiny.copasi.org/ and the source code at https://github.com/copasi/shinyCOPASI.

Deep neural networks are fundamentally altering the landscape of how data and physical laws are combined, resolving complex problems in physics and engineering that had proven insurmountable with conventional methods. Nevertheless, evaluating the accuracy of NN-based predictions proves more complicated than traditional methods. This difficulty arises from not only the inherent randomness in statistical samples used to train the NN, but also the inherent uncertainties in the input data and physical equations themselves, limitations of the training data, and the overfitting that can occur when an NN is fitted to noisy data. This problem is compounded by the propensity for NNs to behave as highly expressive 'black boxes,' obscuring the underlying physical mechanisms. This work aims to develop a comprehensive framework for quantifying and mitigating uncertainties associated with NN-based inference, drawing on techniques from probabilistic inference, surrogate modeling, and surrogate-assisted design. By treating uncertainty as a quantifiable property that can be propagated, we develop methods for quantifying uncertainties and identifying critical factors that can be utilized for optimization. Four real-world applications in engineering and physics are presented to illustrate our framework in practice, including quantifying random uncertainties in image denoising, reducing experimental costs in computer graphics by leveraging NN surrogates, resolving ill-posed inverse problems in the analysis of extracellular electrical fields, and enhancing numerical stability in complex biochemical reaction systems.

We are investigating quantum group analogues of the free group factors' radial subalgebras, specifically those of class functions, within the context of compact quantum groups. The radial function algebra of a given compact quantum group is defined as the set of all functions from the unit circle to the given quantum group that are both continuous and of finite support. The specific case of the free wreten algebra related to a unipotent supergroup follows naturally from this construction. The key innovation here involves establishing the equivalence of two different notions of compactness for radial function algebras, depending on the type of inclusion (quasi-split or non-quasi-split).

Policy iteration comes with computational drawbacks in large-scale Markov decision processes due to a local quadratic contraction rate and the cost of resetting the entire system in each iteration. To circumvent these limitations, we propose a direct application of the Newton-Schulz method for policy evaluation, resulting in a contraction rate of at most O(1), and a significantly reduced computational overhead compared to traditional methods. Moreover, we introduce a crucial insight that enables contraction without requiring the reset of the entire system. Consequently, our approach enables the efficient evaluation of large policies on a wide range of grid-world and continuous-state MDP examples.

Consider a weighted directed graph, denoted as $\mathcal{D}$, and the edge ideal associated with it, labeled as $I(\mathcal{D})$. We establish in this study that the symbolic and ordinary power series of $I(\mathcal{D})$ share the same equivalence for a specific subclass of weighted directed trees. Moreover, the paper also identifies both the required and sufficient conditions under which the symbolic and ordinary power series of oriented line segments exhibit the same behavior.

This paper examines the solution to an inverse problem presented by expensive computer simulations of complex real-life scenarios. Specifically, researchers focused on an expensive hydrological model designed to generate realistic data for Athens, Georgia, USA. To efficiently handle the large datasets produced by such simulators, an approach involves first selecting key points to approximate the output, and then applying a specialized method to estimate optimal input parameters at those points, while accounting for any uncertainty in the solution. A comprehensive simulation-based study compares the proposed technique with other established methods on a range of synthetic and real-world scenarios.

Research has shown that certain distributional assumptions are required to guarantee the reliable learnability of complex concepts when evaluating a robust model's accuracy and considering the influence of random example examinations. Our investigation of the strongest possible distribution assumptions necessary for reliable learnability reveals that certain common assumption types do not lead to robust learnability, while others, such as the assumption that the concept being learned is uniformly distributed over all possible concepts, do result in robust learnability. Our work also examines the impact of altering the conditions of local fairness and completeness on the robust learnability bounds. Additionally, we analyze the effects of changing the nature of local fairness from categorical to continuous, as well as the implications of allowing the model's classifier to take on probabilities other than 0 or 1.

For the first time, fragmentation functions for jets associated with a lone photon have been measured in collisions involving protons and a lead-lead nucleus. This analysis used data from the CMS detector at the CERN LHC, operating at a proton-proton center-of-mass energy of 5.02 TeV. The observations were based on 25 nanobarns of lead-lead and 27 picobarns of proton-proton collisions. The study yielded a statistical sample of 1.3 million jets. The measurements are presented for two different ranges of rapidity and three different ranges of transverse momentum. The study found that fragmentation functions for jets in the most central of lead-lead collisions differ from those of proton-proton collisions. However, these differences are only evident within specific regions of the jet trajectory and its transverse momentum. The study also found that fragmentation functions for jets in less central lead-lead collisions are similar to those of proton-proton collisions.

Recent research involving Feynman integrals has highlighted the significance of Apéry-type inverse binomial series. Building upon previous findings that non-alternating central binomial series could be solved using level four multiple zeta values, we now show that alternating versions require level eight and can be solved using an alternative approach. This involves the substitution of hyperbolic trigonometric 1-forms for their standard trigonometric counterparts.

Follow-up research on WISEA J153429.75-104303.3, previously reported by Meisner et al in 2020, has yielded an assortment of new optical and near-infrared photometric measurements. These new observations were obtained with the 2MASS, All Sky Mid-infrared Atlas (AMIA) and Gaia datasets. Gaia's data specifically revealed the object's low luminosity relative to its location in the color space, with its blue near-infrared slope indicating the presence of dust freelessly gravitational settling within a thin atmosphere. Its exceptionally red near-infrared color, coupled with its bright J -band and faint W1-band, differentiates it from typical Y dwarfs. Our estimates of its effective temperature puts it at 2210±100 K. Considering its large angular separation from the Sun (as seen from Gaia parallax measurements) and lack of X-ray emission (as observed with Chandra), WISEA J1534-1043 appears to be free from contamination. It has the distinction of being the coolest known source apart from the Y dwarf family members. Its low parallax measurement implies it is likely part of the local solar neighborhood. Given its faint optical/nIR flux relative to its large distance, the Gaia mission provides crucial constraints on its atmospheric composition. Its spectrum is most accurately described by a model consisting of dusty atmosphere with very low surface gravity and solar metallicity, featuring the presence of methane, ammonia, hydrogen de

The initial production measurement of various particles such as pions, kaons, 
protons and $\phi$ mesons in midrapidity for Xe-Xe collisions at 5.44 TeV
is reported. Extracted transverse momentum spectra and $p_{\rm T}$-integrated yields 
are analyzed across several centrality intervals. A comparative study of Xe-Xe and 
Pb-Pb collisions reveals similar trends in the dependence of charged-particle 
multiplicity on the flow in Xe-Xe, Pb-Pb, and pp collisions at 5.02 TeV. 
Additionally, the study includes an examination of the suppression patterns of 
these measured particles in Xe-Xe and Pb-Pb collisions.

We develop a novel, numerically efficient approach to solving DGLAP equations for single and double parton distribution functions by leveraging Chebyshev interpolation techniques. This method enhances numerical precision with a reduced number of grid points for PDF evolution, achieving improved efficiency. The DPD evolution process is also accelerated using the same Chebyshev interpolation framework. The proposed method's effectiveness is demonstrated across a range of PDF and DPD sets, with validation for NNLO DGLAP kernels.

Specimens made of Martian and Lunar soil substitutes in various compositions were created and subjected to isostatic pressing, after which they were sintered in a laboratory simulator of the Martian and Lunar surfaces to determine the compressive strength of these materials. The experiments were conducted under conditions mimicking 1/6 and 3/8 gravitational forces, respectively, while also simulating the reduced atmospheric pressures on the Martian and Lunar surfaces. The results showed that a key factor influencing the strength of these materials is the sintering temperature, particularly within a critical range of approximately 1300 to 1330 K. At these temperatures, the compressive strength of these materials was found to be sufficient to support loads equivalent to the weights of several kilograms per square centimeter. The effects of reduced gravity and atmospheric pressure were found to have a negligible impact on the sintering behavior or mechanical properties of these materials. Additionally, it was observed that increasing the fraction of metallic oxides in these samples generally resulted in higher compressive strengths, although the maximum strength was found to occur when the fraction of metallic oxides was between 60% and 70%. The findings of these experiments provide new insights and can contribute to the development of construction materials for future Lunar and Martian settlements.

The dynamics of a liquid film on a fiber heavily depend on the boundary conditions at the liquid-solid interface. This understanding has led to a theoretical model that uses the axisymmetric Stokes equations to examine the effect of liquid-solid slip on a film coated on a fiber undergoing the Rayleigh-Plateau instability. The results show that when slip is factored in, the characteristic exponent for perturbations in a stationary film increases by a factor of 1 plus the product of the Prandtl and Bond numbers. Below a certain threshold, the presence of slip amplifies waves on the film surface, leading to a faster capillary wave speed in relation to the Laplace pressure. A comprehensive study was also conducted on drop formation through a fiber, which revealed that the role of slip becomes substantial only at a small range of values for the Prandtl number and that its impact can be significant even at very low values of the Bond number.

The $\Lambda$CDM model's predicted star formation history can be assessed through a direct measurement of a single hydrogen recombination line, such as the Brackett-$\gamma$ (Br$\gamma$) or Brackett-$\beta$ (Br$\beta$) lines, in a large population of galaxies across various redshifts. By comparing these two lines, a factor that takes into account the characteristics of star-forming galaxies varies, allowing for a prediction to be tested. We use data from 1.4 MHz wide channels over 35 hours for 183 galaxies at $z<1.5$, providing reliable measurements of Br$\gamma$ and robust upper limits for Br$\gamma$. Analyzing the complete sample at $z<0.25$, a 10\% deviation from the predicted relationship between the specific star formation rate (sSFR) and the ratio of Br$\gamma$ to H$\alpha$ is found, however, this agreement breaks down at higher redshifts with significant discrepancies in sSFR observed at $z\sim1$ for the comparison of Br$\gamma$ and H$\alpha$. Moreover, the 158$\pm$35% uncertainty in the predicted sSFR at $z\sim0.5$ due to the use of the 1D versus 2D relationship between the ratio of Br$\gamma$ to H$\alpha$ and sSFR is found, implying a considerable impact of spatial variations in the

This is the initial paper in a two-part series aimed at categorizing a substantial number of the type II quantum subgroups within the specified categories $\mathcal{C}(\mathfrak{sl}_{r+1},k)$ established by Fraydoomand, Fraydoomand, and Kaouache. In this particular study, we delve into the characteristics of the type II quantum subgroups, denoted as $U_{r,(m,nq)}(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_{2})$, where $(m,nq)$ represents a pair of integers. Our research specifically focuses on the 1-dimensional irreducible local modules for each $U_{r,(m,nq)}(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_{2})$. We establish that the braided auto-equivalences of these local modules fall into 16 distinct types, with eight of these being unique and the remaining eight being identical to previously classified categories $\mathcal{C}(\mathfrak{sl}_{r+1},k)$. Four exceptional instances are identified where the braided auto-equivalences exhibit exceptional properties. We then employ the concept of centralizers to determine the type II quantum subgroups for each of these eight unique categories. Our research results in a comprehensive classification of the type II quantum subgroups of the form $U_{r,(m,nq)}(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_{2})$. In the

The Fisher-KPP equation, a reaction-diffusion equation, was first introduced by Fisher for modelling allele spread within genetic populations, but also by Kolmogorov for a broader range of applications. Applying an innovative approach for tackling non-linear partial differential equations provides a distinctive approximate solution to the Fisher-KPP equation, which, however, defies initial intuition. Although the solution respects the maximum principle, a breakdown occurs once time surpasses zero, leading to a significantly higher peak than initially anticipated.

This work addresses the UbiComp 2021 Challenge presented by the 11th International Workshop on Frontiers of Speech Science and Technology, focusing on classifying handwritten mathematical terms into four categories: function, constant, space, and special. A binary classifier is developed to achieve high accuracy rates by tackling the tasks of single-character classification and character combination classification separately. The proposed system achieves 92.15% accuracy when classifying individual characters and reaches 93.33% accuracy when classifying all characters, including spaces.

This paper introduces an innovative method for duration modelling in statistical parametric speech synthesis by training a recurrent model to generate phone transition probabilities frame-by-frame. Unlike traditional approaches that rely on specific distribution types and mean durations for synthesis, this new approach can model any distribution on non-negative integers. We explore a median-based output generation strategy, which offers advantages such as being more representative, robust to training data irregularities, and enabling incremental synthesis. Evaluations demonstrate that this method surpasses existing benchmark techniques in the accuracy of its frame-level predictions.

Species distribution analysis can be effectively addressed using Bayesian inference, which allows for incorporating various factors that could influence the fit of species distribution models. However, introducing these variables increases the computational burden, making Bayesian inference impractical for large datasets. This study develops an innovative method to address this limitation, which enables fitting species distribution models with spatial autocorrelation structures on a massive scale. The approach utilizes random forests to create predictive models for species presence/absence and develops residual plots to identify patterns in the data. Based on these findings, appropriate spatial autocorrelation structures are selected and incorporated into a Bayesian framework for model comparison and estimation. The proposed method is highly flexible, allowing for the selection of multiple spatial structures within a single model. This approach is implemented in a publicly available R package called SpAuto, which is available on CRAN.

Due to a lack of dermatologists, patients experience long waiting times for dermatologic care. Moreover, studies have shown that general practitioners make fewer accurate diagnoses compared to artificial intelligence. The Skincare project aimed to develop an innovative diagnostic solution bridging the gap between dermatologists and AI by facilitating real-time, interactive learning from human experts. The project's key advancements lie in the design of an easy-to-use, web-based system enabling medical professionals to educate AI models in image analysis, particularly in diagnosing malignant skin lesions. The Skincare platform offers several essential features: a user-friendly interface for effortless lesion selection by experts, a study mode allowing human experts to guide AI in making diagnoses, a training mode enabling the fine-tuning of models by humans, and a built-in database of high-quality images. Following the prototype's development, a comprehensive evaluation was conducted with dermatologists to gather feedback on the design and functionality of the platform. The findings indicated that dermatologists required a simpler interface for specifying lesion locations and desired additional capabilities in guiding unexperienced AI models. Based on these insights, the Skincare platform was refined and is now presented as a reliable solution for training and deploying deep learning models in image analysis, specifically in diagnosing cutaneous melanoma.

To capture the intrinsic variability of type Ia supernovae from limited spectral data, a novel method is developed by combining a probabilistic autoencoder with a mixture of normal distributions. This approach, applied to the spectrum of four supernovae with multiple observations, reveals insights into the temporal evolution of each event. Furthermore, it enables the extraction of key features, such as the time of peak brightness, a normalized symmetry index, and spectral features, which can inform about variability and potential biases in cosmological measurements, without referring to an absolute magnitude scale. It is found that peak brightness times can be accurately predicted from a single spectrum, with a scatter similar to that of current Hubble-based cosmology predictions for the luminosity distance. Variability in spectral features is observed and potential corrections for cosmological analyses are suggested. This approach can be extended to future supernova spectrum datasets, such as those expected from the JWST, to understand and mitigate the impact of variability on cosmological parameter estimation.

A massive neutral gas outflow has been observed in a gravitationally lensed star-forming galaxy. The outflow is visible in a narrow band of OH emission, which is likely produced by gas escaping a star-forming region. The outflow is surrounded by a much larger area of hydrogen gas and is embedded within a massive dust cloud. The outflow's direction is likely influenced by the outflow's own pressure and/or magnetic forces rather than external forces. The outflow's atomic gas mass has been estimated to be around 15 million times the mass of the sun. The outflow is also thought to be moving at a speed of around 700,000 kilometers per hour. The outflow is not visible in a different observation of the galaxy made with a different filter. The outflow may be surrounded by a shell of gas that is visible in a different observation of the galaxy made with a different filter. The outflow could be responsible for carving out a hole in the gas around the galaxy. The outflow may eventually be able to escape the galaxy through a hole in the gas around the galaxy. The outflow could be an important key to understanding how star-forming galaxies are limited by their atomic gas supplies.

The movement of dense particles in a turbulent plume under gravity-driven flow has been observed in experiments, with the plume rising or falling depending on the balance between upward and downward forces. When the weight of the particles exceeds their lift capacity, a mantle of lighter fluid forms around them, creating a localized area of negative buoyancy. This area can cause surrounding fluid to sink, drawing in ambient fluid and potentially altering the plume's shape. Most studies on dense particle flows assume the plume has a symmetrical cross-sectional structure, which may not always be the case when considering the effects of orientation and gravity on particle transport. In this study, we investigate the effects of a non-uniform buoyancy flux on the transport of dense particles in a confined space using numerical models. The results show that the direction of the buoyancy flux has a significant impact on the formation of a sedimentary layer, particularly in terms of fluid entrainment and layer thickness. In contrast, the impact of orienting the buoyancy flux along the vertical axis is relatively minimal. Based on these findings, we propose a revised expression for the maximum thickness of the sedimentary layer, which can help simplify the analysis of dense particle flows in a range of geophysical and engineering applications.

Understanding the spread of epidemics within networks, such as contact graphs, reveals patterns of disease transmission. However, assuming only pair-wise interactions oversimplifies the complex human interactions it aims to model. As a more comprehensive framework, hypergraphs enable the representation of multi-person contacts. By translating existing contact graphs into hypergraphs and adding theoretically possible interactions that aren't assumed in the original model, we investigate the spread of diseases on these extended networks. Specifically, we apply the mean-field theory to study the stability of equilibrium states and identify thresholds for critical perturbations. Applying our approach to models of college students, faculty, and staff, we analyze the consequences of increasing connectivity levels and find that extending hypergraphs can lead to a decrease in the minimum contact level required for disease propagation, albeit with certain conditions.

Recent breakthroughs in understanding 2D magnetic semiconductors, exemplified by the layered ferromagnet CrI$_3$, have generated significant enthusiasm due to their potential to integrate spin and charge control within an electronic interface. Although CrI$_3$ exhibits exceptional properties, its inherent characteristics are compromised by defects resulting from exposure to air, research on its electronic properties remains contentious. To overcome these challenges, we employed an ultra-high vacuum to study CrI$_3$ prepared on an SiO$_3$ substrate. Our findings indicate the presence of sizeable ferromagnetic moments in both single and few-layer CrI$_3$ samples even in the absence of external contamination. The research identifies two types of spontaneous magnetization: one due to the arrangement of ferromagnetic Cr vacancies and the other stemming from the alignment of adjacent Cr layers. Moreover, an electric field was observed to significantly influence the magnetization of CrI$_3$. The research offers fresh insights into the properties of magnetic semiconductors, paving the way for the development of innovative spin-electronics and the precise manipulation of magnetic order in these materials.

For solar-type stars, distinct differential rotation patterns emerge based on their Rossby number. Low-R stars exhibit near-polar equatorial acceleration, whereas high-R stars display rotation rates that gradually increase from the poles to 60 degrees. This study aims to provide a theoretical explanation for these observations, focusing on how they are influenced by the differential rotation itself. Our approach relies on solving the Charbonneau and Blondin model, which involves treating the differential rotation as a nonlinear problem, dependent on the latitude and time. Our results show excellent agreement with observations, particularly in terms of the shape and location of the differential rotation gradient. Additionally, we predict that, for low-R stars, the rotation rates will continue to increase towards 90 degrees, although our model slightly underestates the rates observed at 60 degrees.

Deep multimodal learning using K-fan deep Boltzmann machines offers a novel neural network architecture capable of handling multiple input types. Unlike conventional deep learning models, which process each modality in isolation before combining them, our system enables direct two-way communication between modules. As a result, dependencies between different input types are accurately captured. Additionally, the model can capture high-level, complex relationships between inputs in an unsupervised manner. In this research, we introduce a K-fan deep structure model, derived from the existing deep Boltzmann machine, and develop two algorithms for parameter estimation in the new structure. Subsequently, we apply the new model to various datasets, achieving superior performance and surpassing existing state-of-the-art results.

The use of model checking has become increasingly essential in validating the correctness of multi-threaded programs. Traditional unit and functional tests are insufficient due to the hidden nature of race conditions, which can evade detection by these tests. The McMini model checker, which is based on DPOR, has been expanded with a mechanism that enables the declaration of novel, fundamental thread operations through C code. The McMini system now includes a powerful module that enables high-level specifications of multi-threaded programs using the CSP-Omega formal language. This module enhances McMini with capabilities that weren't previously available in the original tool, such as the ability to define threads independently and perform independent computations. The McMini system now offers a unique combination of efficient model checking and the ability to write high-level specifications, making it an advanced, versatile tool for the model checking of multi-threaded programs.

The globally prevalent messaging app, WhatsApp, holds a prominent position in private conversations. Nonetheless, its closed nature hinders the capacity for external information to enter the conversations or leave the platform, with a significant outcome - misinformation spreads rapidly. To combat the spread of false information, a machine learning model is developed in this research to classify text as genuine or deceptive, with a particular focus on Romanized Hindi to combat misinformation in India. An updated version of the FastText model, utilizing a larger Hindi language dictionary, is designed to address the shortage of large,,labeled datasets in the Hindi language. When put to use in a dataset translated from Hindi, the model demonstrates superiority to its competitors, with performance enhancements of 2-4%.

We analyze a general branching population where individual lifetimes are independent and identically distributed with arbitrary distributions, and individuals give birth to new ones at random times following a Poisson process independently from each other. The population's frequency spectrum is studied at arbitrary time points up to a fixed age, based on a large population limit, and its asymptotic distribution is identified as a continuous process governed by a stochastic differential equation, which can be further reduced to a family of ordinary differential equations in a specific scaling regime.

The primary goal of our spoofing countermeasure system is to identify artificial effects within spoken input that arise from speech synthesis or voice alteration techniques. We achieve this goal by incorporating a specialized, attentive activation function - the attention rectified linear unit (AReLU) - into our end-to-end system. By selectively amplifying key input characteristics and suppressing irrelevant ones, AReLU enables our system to prioritize artifact-related features. Our proposed system was applied to the logical access task using the ASVSpoof2019 dataset and demonstrated improved performance compared to systems utilizing standard, non-adaptive activation functions.

Supergravity, an extension of the Standard Model with local supersymmetry, may offer insights into the development of the early Universe through inflation.  However, constructing such an inflationary model in the context of an $M_{3}$ theory proves challenging due to the supergravity's constraints.  This letter proposes an solution to this issue by utilizing non-compact geometric data in the $M_{3}$-supergravity framework.  Specifically, we demonstrate that utilizing non-compact $SL(2,{\mathcal H})$ symmetries in the $M_{3}$-supergravity allows for the construction of viable $M_{3}$-inflation models that comply with the theory's constraints.

Nonreciprocal optical systems have diverse applications that manipulate the transmission of light based on its propagation direction. This study examines a distinct class of nonreciprocity related to the correlation of photon pairs rather than the transmission of light. An experiment was conducted and supported by theoretical findings, showing this nonreciprocity through second-order coherence functions of photon pairs created by spontaneous four-wave mixing in a silicon microdisk. Changing the direction of the pump's propagation leads to significant diminishment in coherence functions while maintaining the transmission.

Superconducting quantum circuits are emerging as prominent platforms for quantum computing. For practical applications, it is essential to address material flaws causing decoherence. This study employs terahertz Scanning Near-field Optical Microscopy to analyze the local dielectric characteristics and carrier concentrations in aluminum resonators on silicon substrates, critical components of superconducting quantum processors. Utilizing a vector calibration method, we determine the resonator loss to be influenced by space charges and radiative losses. We also investigate the impact of laser exposure on the loss and find that carriers generated by light can significantly weaken the resonator's quality factor.

A notable outcome of Hausdorff's research is the proof that the real line can be divided into a countable number of distinct Borel sets. This paper demonstrates that each Borel set within one of these partitions contains a subset consisting of a countable collection of closed intervals. Consequently, a real number $x$ can be assigned to each Borel set $B$ from the partition, such that $x$ belongs to $B$. Additionally, $x$ can be chosen such that its square root is also contained within $B$. This choice is further constrained to ensure that the selected numbers $x$ do not repeat values. As a result, there exists a sequence of distinct real numbers $x_1, x_2, \ldots$, all less than 2, such that for each Borel set $B$ from the partition, either $x_i$ or its square root $\sqrt{x_i}$ belongs to $B$. This sequence is countable because the partition consists of countable sets. Consequently, for any given real number $b$, the set $\{x \leq b\}$ can be shown to contain only a finite number of variants. This property implies that for any given real number $b$, the sequence $\sqrt{x_i}$ mod $2\pi$ coincides with the sequence $e^{i\theta_i}$ where $\theta_i$ are restrictions of $x_i$ to the interval $[0

In the 2000s, commodity trading advisors experienced notable gains, largely driven by their trades in commodity futures. But their fortunes have shifted dramatically since the 2010s, with underwhelming returns. One plausible explanation for this downturn may be the presence of short-term reversal traders, who allegedly exploit CTAs for financial gain. In a recent study, an artificial market model was devised to investigate a different query: whether short-term traders can influence commodity trading advisors and their performance. The research findings indicate that short-term traders have a negligible impact on both their counterparties and the overall market. Additionally, their activities do not seem to affect the commodity trading advisors' performance or as an explanation for their recent underperformance.

Identifying the application protocol is a crucial process in network security monitoring that demands a quick and accurate assessment to support detailed inspection. Although pinpointing the application protocol can be challenging, solely relying on static characteristics like port numbers can be insufficient due to shifting standards and ephemeral communications. In this paper, we introduce a new approach that dynamically identifies application protocols in real-time, analyzing network traffic patterns and anomalies in conjunction with machine learning. Our proposed method relies on flow data and a sliding window approach, utilizing both traditional and modern machine learning techniques for classification. By comparing our approach with existing static methods, we demonstrate that real-time training and classification can effectively identify application protocols with exceptional results, particularly for protocols like HTTP and HTTPS that pose difficulties in detailed protocol analysis.

Electrostatic gating limits the flow of electrons in integrated circuits. Another potential means of information transport, magnons derived from spin waves in magnetic materials, is difficult to regulate. However, we demonstrate the ability to control magnons through electrical means by incorporating a graphene layer into a magnetic structure. The graphene acts as an insulating layer due to graphene-benzene-graphene interface and enables the coupling of electrical signals with magnons. Utilizing a series resistance in the graphene, we are able to modulate the magnon frequency and produce electrical magnon spin-precession. This discovery marks the first instance of electrical magnon control and paves the way for novel magnonic devices and more complex magnon electronics.

A beneficial approach to improving model performance while safeguarding user data privacy exists in using localised data for machine learning model development, specifically through federated learning.  By conducting experiments with FL scenarios and incorporating Shanno's method for gradient updates, quasi-Newton methods such as the Broyden-Fletcher-Robinson algorithm, the quasi-Newton method of its variant with curvature approximation by the Hessian approximation, and the natural and unconditional variants of the Quasi-Newton Federated Learning algorithm have been tested.  Our study compares the performance of these algorithms in achieving optimal results with minimal communication steps, highlighting the difficulties posed by the differences in data distribution among users.

A comprehensive theoretical model is offered in this paper for analyzing high-dimensional entangled systems, specifically the Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger state. Initially, we apply our approach to measure a complete three-photon GHZ state across three dimensions and then extend it to multi-photon systems within higher dimensional settings. In our model, both hyperentanglement of photons and the quantum Fourier transform are employed. The proposed solution can be applied to experimentally detect high-dimensional GHZ entanglement.

This research paper delves into the problem of uplink channel estimation in multi-user systems assisted by intelligent-reflecting-surfaces with limited trainable elements. A reduced computational method is proposed to efficiently estimate the large uplink channel matrix. By breaking down the problem into smaller sub-problems and leveraging a centralized optimization approach with individual objectives, effective channel estimation is achieved. Key outcomes include minimal performance degradation and reduced computational load.

This study analyzes data from an online monitoring system of U.S. local news to explore connections between COVID coverage, regional case and death rates, and characteristics of news outlets and their audiences. Using a distinct dataset of over 750,000 articles from over 300 outlets between April 2020 and February 2021, our results show that local news outlets initially covered COVID at a rate influenced by national death rates but ultimately tied to their own case counts. Furthermore, our research reveals that news COVID coverage is linked to the size of the audience and is influenced by the geography and socioeconomic characteristics of the audience, as well as the news outlet's reputation and existing health infrastructure.

The fundamental ability to count is a prime example of humans' innate capacity for abstract thinking. In this ability, there's typically a notable turning point where children rapidly grasp and master counting techniques. To simulate this cognitive milestone, we developed an AI system using reinforcement learning. By testing this system with the 'give-N' task - where it's given a binary vector and has to pick 'N' items - we discovered that it showed a similar inflection point in learning. Furthermore, our AI, built using the modular network structure known as the ESBN, was able to learn an understanding of 'one-to-one correspondence', a concept essential to counting. When we combined this AI with a simple search algorithm, it successfully solved the 'give-N' task even with high levels of noise.

Bloom filters provide quick approximations of set membership while consuming minimal memory. These filters help engineers prevent time-consuming actions, such as accessing a disk or the network. A potential substitute for Bloom filters is the cuckoo filter, which often needs less storage and processes information faster. A different solution, the Bloomier filter, exists but is hardly ever utilized. This study presents an enhanced variant of the Bloomier filter, dubbed the Array of Hashes Filter, which requires less storage and processing time than the Bloomier filter. This innovation arises from reducing computations using modular matrix addition and designing hashes that produce consistent output for identical inputs. This is achieved by employing multi-level hash approaches, combining them with random linear combinations in the final stage, all of which yield equivalent results in the mod n array. This design results in repeated elements in the array mod n when processing identical inputs, which in turn enables early detection of probable membership in a set. This finding leads to the development of a new algorithm for Array of Hashes Filters as well as the optimal Array of Hashes Tables. This research further explores ways to minimize the number of computations and array dimensions by analyzing the likelihood of encountering duplicate elements in mod n arrays, determining this probability to be extremely low. This study also presents a method to construct a general-purpose mod n array using random elements, which provides the expected performance of early detection for probable membership in a set. This design results in repeated elements in the array mod n array and enables early detection of probable

A significant result in convex geometry states that the positive product of two mixed volumes equals the mixed volume of their respective section bodies, a finding originally attributed to Bernshtein, followed by multiple proofs from various experts. We unreservedly offer an alternative demonstration of this relationship. Moreover, our method provides a straightforward validation of a more comprehensive statement initially proposed by McMullen, which describes the relationship between the mixed Krulller product of two polytopes and the mixed volume of their normalized Dehn invariant.

Key concepts employed include the notion of normality and its association with the mixed Krulller product, originally introduced by Engstr\"om et al., and a decomposition theorem for convex bodies, which can be derived from a method developed by Reisner and Yuzvinskii.

A new approach aims to derive market trend insights from dynamic price equations, specifically those that describe how future prices converge to optimal values, thereby maximizing trading volume per unit of time. This methodology stands out for its inherent ability to select a suitable time frame, which is automatically identified by analyzing past market activity and determining the state of highest trading efficiency. To facilitate trend analysis, both historical and forecasted price data are considered, with past prices represented by lagging values and forecasted prices represented by advancing values.

This work presents FLVoogd, a refined federated learning technique that allows servers and clients to cooperatively prevent Byzantine attacks while maintaining user anonymity. Specifically, servers utilize DBSCAN with k-nearest neighbors to identify suspicious activity, while clients employ a customized batched MC Dropout training method. By integrating these strategies, FLVoogd offers enhanced attack detection capabilities and improves model robustness, all while preserving user data confidentiality.

Autonomous driving technology is advancing rapidly with the support of advanced simulation tools. One key aspect of this research is training agents using reinforcement learning methods. However, generating a large amount of experience data necessary for these training efforts is extremely challenging in a real-world setting. This problem can be overcome by utilizing simulated environments. We have developed a high-quality autonomous driving simulator built with Unreal Engine 4, featuring both a prototypical vehicle design and sophisticated tracking technology. This comprehensive simulation is able to replicate real-world conditions, including diverse road layouts, weather conditions, and pedestrian behaviors, all while providing a seamless and immersive user experience.

Significant progress in deep learning technology has enabled the creation of more convincingly authentic deepfakes, which have sparked interest across multiple sectors due to their vast potential applications, despite raising serious societal and security risks. This chapter examines the advancements and difficulties in the production and identification of deepfakes, and also explores the potential solutions to improve the resilience of deepfake detection for a broad range of media, such as real-world images and videos. Furthermore, it proposes future research directions for tackling deepfake-related issues.

The search is on for exoplanets with properties similar to those of Earth, and which could potentially support life. Our research focuses on the habitability of sub-Neptune-sized exoplanets, which provides an ideal starting point for exploring these celestial bodies. To determine habitability, we consider two key factors: whether the planet's surface receives enough energy from its star to sustain liquid water, and which type of atmosphere it possesses. By creating a statistical model using data from various sources, we developed an equation that represents the distribution of habitable sub-Neptune-sized exoplanets. By applying this equation to specific star types, we can predict the likelihood of finding such planets in those systems and also compare their numbers to those of Earth-like planets. Using these predictions, we can estimate how many Earth-like planets might exist in the Milky Way.

Inspired by the classic McCulloch-Pitts model, we examine a binary neural network consisting of $N$ input neurons, connected to a single output neuron, with the former influenced by an external sequence of $T$ stimuli. The weights in the connections between the input neurons are uneven, with some strengthening sequence learning. We present analytical findings for the optimal optimal optimal weight configuration that enables successful sequence learning. Additionally, we offer an insight into the general binary neural network architecture, consisting of $M$ input neurons and $N$ output neurons, with fixed $T$ and titerate applications of sequence and neural input.

This paper reports on the findings from the 2022 Out-Of-Vocabulary (OOV) challenge.
The competition highlighted an underinvestigated area in Optical Character Recognition (OCR) technology: accurately reading previously unseen text in real-world images during model training.
The dataset compiled for the competition comprises a diverse collection of 326,187 images, encompassing 4,949,364 text instances.
To address the challenge, a distinct validation and test set was created, comprising scene text that was not present in the training data.
The competition featured a single system-level evaluation, where each contribution was evaluated as a comprehensive system, aligning with the Out-Of-Vocabulary framework.
The receiving distribution of the competition entries was 88% vector representations, 8% word-level, 4% character-level, and 3% other distributions.
The outcomes reveal that the traditional end-to-end sequence-to-sequence OCR architecture is ill-suited for out-of-vocabulary tasks.
Some notable methods even failed to recognize individual word IDs, indicating a need for more research in this area.
The competition's software, as well as the compiled dataset, is openly accessible at https://vision.github.io/ooov2022/index.html.

A specific type of chaos expansions can effectively analyze differential equations with uncertain factors by approximating random equilibrium states associated with such equations. This study integrates principles from validated calculations to provide precise error assessments alongside findings about chaos expansions representing random equilibrium states. This approach also develops a new framework for validated tracking, which entails accurately calculating separate solution branches in parameter-dependent systems and generalizes seamlessly to multi-parameter tracking. To demonstrate the proposed methodology, this research achieves the precise calculation of random equilibrium cycles in the Lorenz system, as well as solution branches and 2-dimensional planes of steady states in the Swift-Hohenberg equation.

The increased use of sensors in industrial settings has led to the widespread collection of high-dimensional data, despite this comes with its own set of difficulties. Notably, there's a significant challenge in the computational complexity of some machine learning methods used for data monitoring, which can be a significant limitation in large-scale applications. Furthermore, the high-dimensional data often contains underlying patterns and structures, which can be exploited to improve the efficiency and accuracy of the data monitoring process. This research aims to address these challenges by developing a new approach to change point detection based on a sparse autoencoder that can learn these hidden structures and improve the performance of the detection without compromising computational efficiency. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through simulations and real-world case studies in high-dimensional industrial data analysis.

We have created a detailed analysis of the origins and development of four disrupted galaxies that merged with the Milky Way's outer layers. Our study focuses on the remnants of the Helmi stream, Gaia-Sausage Enceladus, Wukong/LMS-1, and a previously unexplored metal-poor structure known as ECHO. Our findings indicate that ECHO, characterized by its low metallicity and distinct alpha-element abundance ratio, is believed to be a tidal stream originating from a dwarf galaxy that initially had a mass similar to Boötes and consisted of 10 billion solar masses. The ECHO galaxy is thought to have formed approximately 10 billion years ago around a central black hole with a mass of approximately 100,000 solar masses. The galaxy's development is attributed to a central supermassive black hole driving star formation and triggering the formation of stars in young, rotating disks. In contrast, the Gaia-Sausage Enceladus and Wukong/LMS-1 galaxies are known to have had a more dynamic history, with a mass estimated for Gaia-Sausage Enceladus of 10 billion solar masses and a mass estimated for Wukong/LMS-1 of 3 billion solar masses. The two galaxies are believed to have interacted with a massive galaxy, with the interaction causing a tidal collision that led to their incorporation into the Milky Way.
